overview: Black answers 3.d5 by locking the centre with ...e5 and ...d6, accepting a cramped position behind a solid pawn chain. After 4.Nc3 d6 5.e4 Be7 6.Nf3 O-O 7.Be2 the centre is closed; White has more space and plays on the queenside with b4 or Nd2-c4, while Black aims for ...Ne8, ...f5 or ...Nh5, ...f5 on the kingside. It is a slow, strategic fight in which Black's bad dark-squared bishop and lack of space are the main issues.

white_ideas.idea: Use extra space with Nd2-c4, a4 and b4 to open the queenside
Keep the closed centre and restrain ...f5 with Nd2 and f3 if needed
Exploit Black's passive pieces and the bad bishop on g7/e7

black_ideas.idea: Break with ...f5 after ...Ne8 or ...Nh5 preparing kingside play
Meet queenside play with ...a6/...b5 breaks and ...Nbd7-c5
Stay compact and wait for White to overreach

typical_structures.structure: Locked centre with White pawns c4/d5/e4 against Black c5/d6/e5

character.notes: Cramped but compact Black set-up, hard to attack quickly; plans are slow.

soundness.notes: Sound though passive; strong players rate it as slightly worse for Black.

structure.notes: Locked pawn chains, play on the wings.

approach.notes: Standard defence, used occasionally by strong players (Petrosian, Ivanchuk).

level.notes: Plans are strategic and need long-term judgement; theory is light.

sublines_that_differ.name: Early ...Bg4 or other sidelines
sublines_that_differ.how: A King's Indian-style set-up with the kingside fianchetto.

character.reason: A compact, locked Black set-up that is hard to break down but cramped.

soundness.reason: Passive but a respected Black defence.

structure.reason: Locked centre with c4/d5/e4 against c5/d6/e5.

approach.reason: Played by strong players now and then, not a system.

level.reason: Slow strategic plans, little forced theory.

plans.reason: White's space and Black's hemmed-in pieces define the structure.
